title: Body found in Cambridge pond, police say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A body was discovered in Fresh Pond, Cambridge, on Tuesday morning, prompting a police investigation.
Preliminary findings suggest the body had been in the water for an extended period, according to the authorities.
The identity of the person and circumstances of the discovery remain unknown as the investigation continues.

title: 6 takeaways from a competitive joint practice for Patriots, Colts
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye led a strong Patriots offense against the Colts, completing 15 of 23 in 11-on-11 drills.
Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez missed practice amid contract negotiations; his status remains uncertain.
Colts exploited Patriots' thin cornerback depth, with Daniel Jones excelling in red-zone drills during practice.

title: This North Shore city was Realtor.com’s hottest ZIP code in 2026
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Peabody, Massachusetts, named the hottest ZIP code for 2026 by Realtor.com, with notable market demand and quick home sales.
Peabody's housing market saw homes listed for a median price of $667,000 and selling 0.07% below the asking price.
Realtor.com ranks ZIP codes by buyer interest; Peabody's 4.1 times the national views and 20-day median market time were highlights.

title: Q&A: A 96-year-old traveler on visiting all 63 national parks with her grandson
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Grandma Joy and Brad Ryan visited all 63 U.S. national parks from 2015 to 2023.
Joy, the oldest person to visit all parks, began traveling with her grandson at age 85.
The pair will discuss their journey and memoir at Harvard Book Store on August 13.

title: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel shares what he’s learned from offseason counseling​
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel discussed offseason counseling sessions focusing on personal and team improvement for the 2026 NFL season.
Vrabel missed Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft for family counseling, impacting Patriots' offseason plans.
Vrabel emphasized ongoing mental fitness preparations with Dr. Jonathan Jenkins for players and staff during the regular season.

title: Worcester officials urge MBTA to improve commuter rail service to and from Boston
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Worcester officials urge MBTA to restore express commuter rail service between Worcester and Boston to meet strict travel time targets.
The new report highlights key issues like aging infrastructure, potential bottlenecks, and the need for improved travel times on the Framingham/Worcester Line.
Worcester leaders express concerns over the Allston Multimodal Project's impact on travel times and advocate for a station layout allowing express routes.

title: One of the rarest basketball cards in the world was pulled in New England on Monday
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: A 1:1 Cooper Flagg Rookie Debut Patch Autograph card was pulled by RhodyBreakers in North Kingstown, Rhode Island.
The card features a jersey patch from Flagg's NBA debut with the Dallas Mavericks and is estimated to be worth up to $5 million.
The Dallas Mavericks offered a package including tickets and memorabilia for the card, but collectors suggest it could sell for more in auction.

title: Review & setlist: Olivia Dean taught Boston how to love at TD Garden
author: Kelly Chan
bullets: Olivia Dean performed at TD Garden in Boston on August 10, 2026, showcasing her album 'The Art of Loving.'
Dean's set included hits like 'Dive,' 'Man I Need,' and featured intimate moments and brass instrumentals.
The concert ended with a confetti blast, highlighting themes of self-discovery and connection in her music.

title: Belmont, Mass., teens arrested after N.H. police chase
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two Belmont, Mass., 18-year-olds were arrested after a police chase on I-95 in New Hampshire.
Driver Justin Jedrey faced felony and misdemeanor charges; passenger Nikol Muka charged with unlawful possession.
Jedrey is in preventive detention until his Aug. 20 court date; Muka released on bail, court date set for Sept. 28.

title: Faneuil Hall managers sue tenants over more than $2 million in alleged unpaid rent
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: J. Safra Real Estate is suing seven Faneuil Hall Marketplace tenants for over $2 million in alleged unpaid rent.
The lawsuits, affecting tenants like FoMu and Boston Sugar Factory, were filed in Suffolk Superior Court from 2024 to 2026.
FoMu disputes claims, citing demolition costs from pest damage; J. Safra investing in marketplace improvements to attract tenants.
